correctness.rationale: For G=C_n square K_m, Cartesian shortest-path distance is d_C(x,y)+1_{p != q}, hence every p-to-q geodesic contains exactly one p-to-q clique/rung edge; n such edges need a_p*a_q>=n distinct selected endpoint pairs for each p<q. The product over all layer pairs plus AM--GM gives |S|>=m sqrt(n). For the upper bound k=ceil sqrt(n), s=min(n,2k+6), the full-vertex case s=n is immediate. For s<n take s distinct anchors T={floor(i*n/s)}, 0<=i<s, in every layer. An L-consecutive-residue interval has at least floor(sL/n) anchors, so the i-th predecessor and j-th successor of each target r lie within ceil(i*n/s) and ceil(j*n/s). Setting h=s/2-2=k+1 gives d_left+d_right <= h*n/s+2 <= n/2 for positive i+j<=h; oriented anchor choices yield h(h-1)=k(k+1)>=n *distinct ordered coordinate pairs* whose shortest cycle arc passes through each target rung. Greedy injection handles all n target rungs per fixed unordered layer pair; pair sets across layer pairs are disjoint. Consecutive anchors have gaps <=ceil(n/s)<=n/2 and cover all rim edges with unused, unique same-layer endpoint pairs. For n=k^2,k>=3, equally spaced k anchors in every layer suffice: the ordered anchor pair (i,d), 0<=i,d<k, is assigned the rung ik for d=0; ik+d for 1<=d<=floor(k/2); and ((i-1) mod k)*k+d for larger d. Each rung in each gap has unique offset, yielding bijection onto k^2 rungs; chosen directed arcs are shortest and same-layer consecutive-anchor paths cover all cycle edges without duplicate unordered endpoints for k>=3. Thus |S|=mk, matching lower bound for all m>=2. Independent implementation tested 268 general parameter pairs (n up to 300), 39 square cases (k up to 15), and 338345 cyclic interval instances, checking all vertex endpoints, exact graph distance, no duplicate unordered endpoint pairs, and edge coverage. The infinite theorem rests on the symbolic argument, not these finite tests.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks use bounded cases and are not an exhaustive verification of arbitrary n,m.
No claim on exact nonsquare value, general optimal leading constant, m=1, or n<3.

The path--clique exact theorem cannot be applied by changing the graph, and the published complete multipartite and grid results concern different domains. The claimed balanced cyclic greedy matching and square-order geodesic assignment are substantive new implications compared with the read prior statements.

value.rationale: The parameterized strong edge-geodetic set of cyclic clique cylinders is a naturally motivated edge-covering graph invariant; the cycle closure removes the linear shortest-path structure used in the known exact P_n square K_m theorem. Uniform two-parameter upper and lower bounds matching in order Theta(m sqrt n), a constructive approximation factor approaching two independent of clique size, and an exact infinite square-cycle subfamily with an explicit geodesic rung bijection are substantial and independently useful. The construction is not a routine substitution or isolated finite table; it handles every m>=2 and all n>=3, although it leaves nonsquare exact values and optimal leading constant open.
residual_risks: Sharp leading constant and exact nonsquare parameter values remain unknown; the main result claims only the proper order and infinite exact subsequence.
